candidates.topic: The Man Who Never Forgot Anything — Hyperthymesia
candidates.teaser: Some people literally cannot forget a single day of their life — and scientists aren't sure if it's a gift or a curse.
candidates.video_title: He Remembers Every Second of His Life
candidates.video_description: A rare neurological condition called hyperthymesia allows certain people to recall every moment of their lives in perfect detail. Scientists have identified fewer than 100 confirmed cases worldwide, and studying them is changing everything we know about memory.
candidates.script: This woman can tell you exactly what she was doing at 3 PM on March 14th, 1987 — without hesitating for a second. A condition called hyperthymesia gives certain people total, involuntary recall of every single day of their lives. Fewer than 100 confirmed cases exist on Earth. They don't choose to remember — the memories play on their own, like an endless loop. Scientists still don't know whether to call it a superpower or a sentence. Would you want to remember everything?

candidates.topic: The Paris Catacombs Hold More Dead Than Living
candidates.teaser: Beneath the streets of Paris, the dead outnumber the living by more than ten to one — and the city is built right on top of them.
candidates.video_title: Paris Is Built Over 6 Million Dead Bodies
candidates.video_description: The Catacombs of Paris stretch over 300 kilometers beneath the city and hold the remains of more than six million people. Originally limestone quarries, they were converted into mass burial sites in the 18th century when Parisian cemeteries started collapsing into basements.
candidates.script: Every café, every boulevard, every metro station in Paris sits directly above six million human skeletons. The Catacombs stretch 300 kilometers beneath the city — longer than the entire Paris Metro system. In the 1780s, overflowing cemeteries were literally collapsing into people's cellars, so authorities moved the dead underground and stacked the bones into walls. Some tunnels have never been fully mapped. Tourists visit a small section. Nobody knows what lives in the rest.

candidates.topic: Trees Communicate and Warn Each Other — Wood Wide Web
candidates.teaser: Forests have a secret underground internet — and trees use it to send warnings, share food, and even sabotage their enemies.
candidates.video_title: Forests Have a Secret Underground Internet
candidates.video_description: Trees are connected through an underground fungal network scientists call the 'Wood Wide Web.' They use it to share nutrients, send chemical distress signals to neighboring trees, and even direct resources toward their own offspring. It's rewriting our definition of intelligence.
candidates.script: The forest you're walking through right now is having a conversation beneath your feet. Trees are linked by a fungal network so complex that scientists named it the Wood Wide Web. A mother tree can identify her own seedlings underground and send them extra carbon through the network. When one tree is attacked by insects, it fires chemical warnings to its neighbors within hours. They respond by producing toxins before the attack even reaches them. So — are trees actually intelligent?

candidates.topic: The Russian Sleep Experiment — Real Government Insomnia Studies
candidates.teaser: Soviet scientists once tested what happens when humans are forced to stay awake for weeks — the real results were disturbing enough without any fiction.
candidates.video_title: Soviets Kept Humans Awake for 30 Days Straight
candidates.video_description: While the famous 'Russian Sleep Experiment' is a horror story, the USSR's real sleep deprivation research was alarming in its own right. Documented Soviet and U.S. military experiments showed that severe sleep deprivation causes hallucinations, organ failure, and eventually death — in as few as 11 days.
candidates.script: After just 11 days without sleep, a human being begins to die — and in the 1970s, governments actually tested how far that line could be pushed. Declassified Soviet and U.S. military records confirm sleep deprivation experiments on both soldiers and civilians. Subjects began hallucinating by day four. By day eight, organ function started deteriorating. The world record, set without coercion, stands at 11 days and 25 minutes — and the man who set it was never quite the same again.

candidates.topic: The Vantablack Color — So Dark It Erases Shape
candidates.teaser: There's a material so dark that your eyes literally cannot process the shape of whatever it covers — it looks like a hole cut into reality.
candidates.video_title: This Color Is So Dark It Breaks Your Eyes
candidates.video_description: Vantablack, developed in 2014, absorbs 99.965% of all visible light. Objects coated in it appear completely flat — your brain cannot detect edges, depth, or dimension. It was originally engineered for space telescopes, but its visual effect is so extreme it has triggered legal battles in the art world.
candidates.script: Coat a crumpled ball of tin foil in this material and it looks like a perfect flat circle — your brain simply cannot process the depth. Vantablack, created in 2014, absorbs 99.965% of all light that touches it. It was built for space telescopes to eliminate lens glare. But when artists tried to use it, one sculptor legally locked every other artist out of the material for years. A single gram costs more than gold. And visually — it looks less like a color and more like a hole cut straight through reality.
